config.measurement: Lane B B1 A/B: incremental (delta) manifest, per docs/design/INCREMENTAL_MANIFEST_FORECAST_2026-09-13.md SS5/SS6
config.control_note: pre-B1/B2, ancestor of both merge commits 391b413 (B1) and 2f95d9f (B2); MANIFEST_FORMAT_VERSION absent, verified before use

b1a.stop_rule: killed at the 2,500,000 ops log line (matched ops between arms); --write-path assert is required to reproduce the pathology -- the default --write-path bulk checkpoints every 50,000 ops and does not

b1c.method: NativeAdapter(store/'native') construction time (the Rust-level NativeStore::open), NOT tgms.open() -- tgms.open additionally replays the event log, a materially larger and different cost

b1d.method: adapter.verify() wall on the treatment store post-b1a

seed.reason: b1a is a deterministic replay of the fixed LDBC SF1 CSV corpus (no RNG); b1b's commitcost harness seeds a 100k-row store deterministically by row index, not by an RNG seed argument -- see scripts/eval_concurrency.py cmd_commitcost

dataset.name: ldbc-sf1-composite-merged-fk-initial-snapshot
dataset.digest_note: no built-store digest applies to a raw CSV corpus (the schema's enum has no such kind); this is sha256 of the sorted (relative_path, size) listing of every file under the initial_snapshot directory -- a structural fingerprint confirming both arms read the identical input, not a content hash of the CSV bytes

F1_manifest_bytes_le_500MB_at_2.5M_ops.measured: treatment manifests = 62,046,913 B (62.0 MB); control (pathology reproduction) = 25,970,987,762 B (25.97 GB); segments ~146.5-146.6 MB both arms

F2_phase_deciles_le_1.2x.measured: manifest_us last/first decile: control 2.09-2.17x, treatment 1.04-1.13x (component PASSES); engine-commit total_us last/first decile: control ~2.07-2.10x, treatment 1.78-1.80x (component FAILS, > 1.2x). Falsifier is an OR of the two components; the total_us component triggers it.

F3_cold_open_le_100ms_at_G10k_K512.measured: treatment NativeStore::open ~8,578-8,649 ms (n=3) at G~10,008 with checkpoint=9,728 + 280 deltas; control (full-manifest parse, format 1) ~1,066-1,071 ms at G~10,014 -- treatment is ~8x SLOWER to open than control, not faster

F4_p50_ge_15pct_below_5.07ms_baseline.measured: treatment engine-commit p50 (total_us) = 5,584 us (5.58 ms), ABOVE the 5.07 ms historical baseline, not >=15% below it (bound was <=4.31 ms); this run's own control p50 was 6,017 us, ~19% above the historical baseline too, so host/data conditions differ somewhat from the original measurement, but the paired treatment vs. this run's control improvement (~7%) also misses 15%

F5_no_invariant_regressions.measured: tests/test_concurrency.py tests/test_native_faults.py tests/test_tcsr_persistence.py: 32 passed, 0 failed on the treatment engine

falsifiers.overall: REFUTED (3 of 5: F2, F3, F4) -- the byte-savings claim (F1) and the invariant-preservation claim (F5) are decisively confirmed, but the CPU/latency claims (F2, F3, F4) are all refuted by the measured data. Per SS5, an Addendum-1-anticipated outcome for F2 (manifest bytes vs. engine-commit CPU are separate claims); F3's magnitude (~86x over bound) and F4's direction (treatment slower than the historical baseline, not just short of the 15% target) were not anticipated by the memo and should be treated as new findings, not noise.
